title: The fibrewise Cohen–Macaulay locus is dense in every fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For $s\in S$ write $X_s$ for the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. The subset $C_s\subseteq X_s$ consisting of the points $x$ for which the fibre local ring $R=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is Cohen–Macaulay is dense in $X_s$: every nonempty open subset of $X_s$ meets $C_s$. Here Cohen–Macaulay means that $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and its depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] equals its Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and a nonempty open subset $O\subseteq X_s$, and choose $x\in O$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], identify $X_s$ homeomorphically with the subspace $f^{-1}(s)$ of $X$. Thus there is an open $W\subseteq X$ with $O=W\cap f^{-1}(s)$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$ containing $s$, and then, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $x\in U\subseteq W\cap f^{-1}(V)$. The induced open $U_s\subseteq X_s$ is nonempty and contained in $O$, and $f(U)\subseteq V$. For an empty fibre the density assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 01IT (affine opens form a basis) and the fibre-topology identification used in Tag 045U

proof.text: For the affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ just chosen, [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives a finite presentation $A\cong R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso] with $Z=X$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, base open $V$, and source open $U$; the inverse image of $V$ in $T$ is all of $T$. Its isomorphism identifies $U_s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(s)\otimes_R A)$. The elementary tensor symmetry $a\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes a$ identifies this ring with $B=A\otimes_R\kappa(s)$. The elements $t_i\otimes1$ generate $B$ as a $\kappa(s)$-algebra: expand each $a\in A$ as a polynomial in the $t_i$, and each tensor as a sum of pure tensors. Thus $B$ is finite type in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

Apply [lem-trf-generic-cm-locus-field] to the finite type $\kappa(s)$-algebra $B=A\otimes_R\kappa(s)$. Since $U_s$ is nonempty, its affine spectrum contains a prime $\mathfrak q$ with Cohen–Macaulay localization $B_{\mathfrak q}$. Let $y\in U_s\subseteq O$ be the corresponding point. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], applied to the affine open $U_s$ of $X_s$ and its affine ring identification, $B_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{X_s,y}$ as local rings. Ring isomorphisms identify ideals, prime chains and regular sequences, so they preserve Noetherianity, Krull dimension and depth as defined in [def-weil-pbc-depth] and [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Hence $y\in C_s\cap O$. Since $s$ and $O$ were arbitrary, $C_s$ is dense in every fibre.

lean.statement: theorem flat_lfp_cm_locus_fibre_dense {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] : ∀ (s : S) (O : Set (f.fiber s)), IsOpen O → O.Nonempty → ∃ x : f.fiber s, x ∈ O ∧ IsNoetherianRing ((f.fiber s).presheaf.stalk x) ∧ (IsLocalRing.depth (R := (f.fiber s).presheaf.stalk x) ((f.fiber s).presheaf.stalk x) : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim ((f.fiber s).presheaf.stalk x)
